FAST

LONDON, Aug 24 : Oil prices slipped more than $1 a barrel on Monday as investors took profits after recent gains and awaited details of expected new U.S. sanctions on Iran, which could further disrupt supplies from the Middle East. Brent crude futures were down $1.55, or 1.64 per cent, to $92.84 at 0911 GMT, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was at $85.02 a barrel, down $2.04, or 2.34 per cent. Both contracts posted a second consecutive weekly gain last week, rising more than 5 per cent, as peace negotiations between the U.S. and Iran stalled, constraining oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, a route that once carried a fifth of global supplies. "Oil slipped after a two-week rally as traders awaited the U.S. plan to economically isolate Iran due later Monday," said Saxo Bank analysts in a note.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who is set to hold a press conference at 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT) on Monday, has threatened to impose "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran. President Donald Trump has also threatened to impose sanctions on Iran's trading partners. "Should the pledged embargo be launched, oil supply from the region will fall," said PVM analyst Tamas Varga, adding that the U.S. would likely tighten its naval blockade against Iranian oil exports and that Iran could retaliate with fresh strikes against oil installations in the Middle East.  Iran has condemned U.S. plans to announce new sanctions and President Masoud Pezeshkian has called for a diplomatic solution. Pakistan's army chief was visiting Tehran on Monday for mediation talks, ahead of the U.S. announcement. Fewer than 20 commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz at the weekend, shipping data showed on Monday, as Iranian and U.S. blockades restrict traffic through the chokepoint for energy shipments. Offers of Iranian crude to Chinese buyers have declined and prices have jumped as the U.S. blockade has cut Tehran's shipments, according to trade sources. However, Iran has granted permission for a number of Iraqi oil tankers to pass through the strait following repeated requests from Baghdad, Iran's state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday. Iraq's SOMO and QatarEnergy both offered crude for loading inside the strait in tenders, trade sources told Reuters.  Brent has climbed back up to around $92 per barrel, from as low as $71 in June, due to inventory draws and a growing sense that Middle East disruptions can last longer, Morgan Stanley analysts said in a note.  The bank increased its Brent forecasts, projecting a peak at $100 in the fourth quarter.

Source: Reuters

Aug 24 : Juventus manager Luciano Spalletti said new signing Randal Kolo Muani has a lot of work to do if he is to recapture his best form after the French forward failed to shine in their 1-0 win at Frosinone Calcio on Sunday. The 27-year-old has returned to Juve for a second spell after spending half a season on loan at the Turin club last year, signing a five-year contract in a deal worth 38 million euros ($44.35 million) earlier this month. Juve have signed the former Paris St Germain forward as a replacement for Dusan Vlahovic following the Serbian's departure to Besiktas. In his first spell at Juve, Kolo Muani scored 10 goals in 22 appearances before PSG loaned to Tottenham Hotspur for the 2025-26 season.

Spalletti told broadcaster DAZN that Kolo Muani should have been on the scoresheet in their Serie A opener on Sunday. Brazilian centre back Gleison Bremer netted the only goal of the game. "We went out and signed him (Kolo Muani), we've looked after him and we know his worth, but he needs to realise he hasn't played for two years and there must be a reason for that," he said. "Sometimes you think you're at an exceptional level, but then you've left something behind and you have to go and get it back. "Kolo knows how to hold onto the ball, find space and is physically strong, but these are the sort of matches where he needs to score goals." Juve next host Parma on Saturday. ($1 = 0.8568 euros)

KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesia has given Malaysian agencies official permission to enter its airspace to conduct cloud seeding operations, Malaysia's environment minister said on Monday (Aug 24), part of both countries' efforts to combat the haze blanketing the region .  Indonesia has been stepping up efforts to slow the spread of haze caused by forest and land fires across several provinces, which this month led to dozens of school closures, including in neighbouring Malaysia.  Malaysia's national disaster management agency and its meteorological department are currently preparing schedules for cloud seeding operations in shared border locations, Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Arthur Joseph Kurup said in a statement.  This will be coordinated with the Indonesian military, he said.

Malaysia was also prepared to offer assistance to Indonesia in extinguishing fires, with any specific requests to be brought to Cabinet for further action, said the minister. Kurup said the two countries would be escalating their firefighting and fire prevention programmes ahead of national holidays in the coming weeks, including the Malaysia Day celebrations in Sarawak state on Sep 16. Sarawak, which borders Indonesia's Kalimantan province on Borneo island, has been worst hit by the haze. Six districts in Sarawak recorded unhealthy air pollution index (API) readings on Monday, according to data released by the environment department.  Unhealthy API levels were also recorded in eight other districts across four states on the Malaysian peninsula, the data showed.

FAST

LONDON/SYDNEY, Aug 24 : Global stocks slipped on Monday and oil prices eased as investors awaited details of threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran, while the Canadian dollar dipped as a trade war loomed with its southern neighbour. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to hold a press conference later on Monday to outline sanctions on Iran, which has shown no sign of relinquishing its control over the vital Strait of Hormuz. Oil futures were down more than 1 per cent ahead of the announcement as some oil traders took profits after big gains last week. The tech sector was on edge for Nvidia's results on Wednesday; investors are aware how hard it will be for the chipmaker to meet stratospheric expectations.

"The big news this week will be Nvidia earnings... The tone of that might drive sentiment into the Nasdaq (market)," said Nutshell Asset Management CIO Mark Ellis. Analysts are generally looking for quarterly revenue to almost double to around $92 billion, with full-year earnings guidance seen in a range of $103 billion to $105 billion. WARSH SPEECH MAY DISAPPOINT Market participants will also be hoping for some clarity on the outlook for U.S. interest rates when Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh speaks in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday, though his well-known aversion to forward guidance could lead to disappointment. "There are several reasons to expect to be underwhelmed," said Bruce Kasman, chief economist at JPMorgan, noting that past chairs have not wanted to front-run Fed decisions at the event. "Warsh will rather likely focus on aspects of his 'regime change' agenda," Kasman added. "As the Fed has already been moving toward shrinking the balance sheet, and the committee gave the balance sheet some attention in the July minutes, that might be the most likely topic for him to expound upon." Markets imply around a 40 per cent chance that the Fed will raise interest rates when it meets on September 16 and are fully priced for a move by December. The odds could change depending on what U.S. inflation figures show this week, with median forecasts for core inflation expected to hold at 3.3 per cent in July.  Warsh is sure to face questions about Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's surprise announcement last week of at least a doubling in bond buybacks, aimed at restraining a rise in yields that was tightening financial conditions in the economy. His efforts have had little success so far, with 30-year yields at 5.2518 per cent, not far from the recent 19-year peak of 5.3371 per cent. U.S.-CANADIAN TRADE WAR European stocks edged 0.1 per cent lower in early trading, following declines across Asia including tech-heavy South Korean shares. On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures fell 0.2 per cent and Nasdaq futures were down 0.7 per cent. The Hong Kong-listed shares of Alibaba slid around 9 per cent after the Chinese e-commerce and cloud computing company launched a $10.2 billion share offer and investors worried about payback from its massive AI spending. fell more than 8 per cent after a record $79 billion shareholder-return plan disappointed investors who had expected a larger share of AI-fuelled cash windfalls.  In currency markets, the dollar added 0.5 per cent against its Canadian counterpart to 1.3837 after Prime Minister Mark Carney said his country would respond to U.S. tariffs with levies of its own as trade talks broke down. Canada will impose tariffs on U.S. steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics, along with some products that the U.S. previously targeted in Canada. The dollar index was up 0.2 per cent to 98.983. The euro dipped 0.1 per cent to $1.16655 after rising 0.9 per cent last week, while the dollar gained 0.1 per cent to 159.2 yen. Gold firmed another 0.8 per cent to $4,640 an ounce, having climbed about 15 per cent for the month so far.

Source: Reuters

BEIJING, Aug 24 : Alibaba officially rolled out its latest AI video generation-model Wan3.0 on Monday with enhanced capabilities after the Chinese internet giant launched a $10 billion share placement to fund rising AI spending. • The new model can generate 30-second videos from documents, spreadsheets, slides and web pages, Alibaba Cloud said in a post on the WeChat platform. • Alibaba said Wan3.0 had been used in short drama and film production, advertising and marketing, tourism promotion and music video creation since a public beta version was launched on August 6. • The release comes a day after Alibaba announced the share sale, the largest-ever primary follow-on offering by a Hong Kong-listed company, as it ramps up spending in the intensifying global AI race. • Alibaba last week reported a 75 per cent plunge in quarterly earnings from a year ago due to soaring AI-related capital expenditure.

JOHANNESBURG, Aug 24 : South Africa have released fullback Quan Horn and prop Boan Venter from the Springbok squad to play for provincial side Lions against New Zealand at Ellis Park on Tuesday. • Venter was named on Monday among the replacements and is in line to make his Lions debut after signing for them, having played for Edinburgh in Scotland. • There could also be a debut for former Springbok loose forward Sikhumbuzo Notshe, who previously played club rugby in France and is also on the bench. • The Lions’ other Springbok squad member, scrumhalf Morné van den Berg, has not been released, increasing his chances of a run out against the All Blacks in Saturday’s second test in Cape Town.

RENNES, France, Aug 24 : Paris Saint-Germain players can ill afford to cruise through the season as coach Luis Enrique warned he expected them to play out of their comfort zone. The PSG coach took off both Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at halftime of their opening game of the new Ligue 1 season, bringing on Mika Godts and Ferran Torres, who scored twice to salvage a point at Stade Rennais on Sunday. "Football is like that. Paris Saint-Germain have won nothing, nothing," he said of the new season where they defend not only their Ligue 1 title but chase a third successive Champions League victory. "If you think about what you've won, you're not going to win anything! There is no credit. You have to show every day, every match, every training session, that you're ready. Otherwise, it's easy to relax and start slipping.

"I wasn't brought up that way. We are always looking to win, and to keep winning, you have to step outside your comfort zone. Is that clear?" PSG, who won the European Super Cup this month but lost the French version to Racing Lens, played a sluggish first half at Rennes and were 2-0 down at the break. But new Spanish signing Ferran Torres, who netted the winner in last month's World Cup final, came on for Dembélé and scored twice to ensure a point for the Parisians. "He wasn't bad, was he? He scored two goals, but I'm happy with everyone who came on in a very difficult match because we had a lot of trouble controlling Rennes in the first half," Luis Enrique said. "They were good on the counterattack and scored two wonderful goals. It was complicated, but it's important for me to see that so many players are ready. "We sign players to go on a long journey with them. It's very positive for him and we're very happy," he said of Ferran Torres' debut. "We're always looking to find the best players for every match. Places in the team will be more difficult to get than last year, and that's our ambition. "I think we had a very good transfer window, and we're still open to different possibilities. Everyone knows how difficult it is for a team to keep winning. And clearly, we still need to improve."

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Christopher Cushing)

Aug 24 : Fabinho is set to link up with ex-Liverpool teammate Mohamed Salah at Trabzonspor after the Turkish Super Lig side posted a photo of the 32-year-old Brazilian wearing their kit onboard a private jet. "A familiar face is waiting for me in Trabzon" said Fabinho in the Trabzonspor social media post. Fabinho joined Saudi Arabia's Al Ittihad in 2023 after his five-year stint at Liverpool and is now a free agent. Egyptian forward Salah also joined Trabzonspor as a free agent earlier this month.

ZANDVOORT, Netherlands, Aug 24 : McLaren have taken a big step forward and Mercedes no longer have the quickest car in Formula One, championship leader Kimi Antonelli said after Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix. McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris celebrated his second win in a row from pole position at Zandvoort, with Antonelli and Mercedes teammate George Russell second and third ahead of Ferrari pair Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc. "We’re clearly not the fastest car anymore on the grid," said Antonelli, who won five races in a row earlier in the season. "We’re probably second or third, at least in today’s race, and McLaren has taken a huge step, especially since Hungary, since the big upgrade package they brought."

Norris, who lost out to Antonelli at the race restart and then had to overtake him on track, questioned that assertion however. "I don’t think it’s true. I think if I didn’t get Kimi when I overtook him, I don’t think I would have won the race," he said. "For once I would give myself a little bit of credit that I feel like I’m doing a better job than everyone, and I think that can also make a difference. "We certainly have a car now capable of beating them ... but I think they have a better all-round performing car than what we do." Zandvoort, and Budapest's Hungaroring before that, played to McLaren's strengths but some of the tracks coming up may be less favourable. Ferrari can be expected to go well at their home grand prix at Monza early next month, with upgrades in the pipeline, while Antonelli faces hefty grid penalties for an engine change. A TOUGHER RIDE Mercedes are still way ahead of Ferrari and McLaren in the constructors' championship and scored more points (46 to McLaren's 43 and Ferrari's 31) than anyone else over the weekend. "We have a strong car in certain areas. It’s not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere," said Norris. "We’re very, very strong in high speed, and that’s the place we’ve improved the car the most, is high-speed performance. No one matches us in high speed, and that’s a good thing. "But the advantage that they (Mercedes) have to us in slow speed is also crazy. And therefore, I don’t have the confidence to say 'yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season. "I know I’ve just won two races in a row and had two poles in a row, but at the minute I don’t have the car I need to fight for a championship," added the Briton, who is 83 points behind Antonelli with another 11 rounds remaining unless the situation in the Middle East forces a calendar change. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said cost-cap restrictions meant Mercedes did not have the money to put developments on the car as fast as they might like to. "We are trying to evenly split that through the season based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points," he told reporters. "So the ride has been a bit tougher than at the beginning of the year." McLaren principal Andrea Stella said he expected Mercedes to accelerate their car's development regardless. "I'm sure their car in the wind tunnel is quite a bit faster than the car they have on track," said the Italian. "And they will want to now convert some of this potential into upgrades that make it to the real car. I'm just pretty sure that they will have upgrades."

Source: Reuters
